note: Must fermented with honey and salt; multi-ingredient, no single plant source beyond grape.
Old austere wine mixed with honey; multi-ingredient preparation.
Honey mixed with water, boiled or unboiled; bee product, no plant source.
General discussion of drinking waters by source and quality.
Sea water used for baths, enemas and fomentations; saline substance.
Boiled sea water with honey (2:1); multi-ingredient preparation.
Wine vinegar; product of the grapevine.
Vinegar, sea salt, honey and water boiled together; multi-ingredient.
Vinegar with brine; multi-ingredient preparation.
Eponymous main ingredient thymos (Thymbra capitata) with salt, barley meal, rue, pennyroyal, vinegar; multi-ingredient.
Vinegar of white skilla (sea squill); standard identification.

headword: ὁ δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς σκίλλης ρἶνος γίνεται οὕτω
note: Wine of dried sea squill (skilla).

headword: οἱ δὲ διὰ θαλάττης οἶνοι ποικίλως σκευάζονται
note: Grape must/raisins mixed with sea water; defined by non-plant additive.
Kydonites/melites from quince (melon kydonion).
Quinces preserved in honey.
Quince honey diluted with water.

headword: ὀ μφακόμελι δὲ σκευάζεται τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον
note: Juice of unripe grapes (omphax) with honey.
Pear wine; also wines of carob (keration), medlar (mespilon) and service-berry (oa).
Dried flowers of wild vine (oinanthe), i.e. Vitis vinifera subsp. sylvestris.
Juice of seedless pomegranates (rhoa).
Dried roses (rhodon) in must; ancient rose usually read as Rosa gallica/damascena group.
Juice of ripe black myrtle berries (myrta).
Branches, leaves and berries of black myrtle (myrsine).

headword: καὶ ὁ σχίνινος δὲ ἐοικότως τῷ μυρσινίτῃ σκευάζεται
note: Schinos (lentisk) wine; terebinth (terminthos) wine made likewise.
Wine of ripe dates (phoinikes).
Trochites/sykites from dried black figs, made in Cyprus.
Wine from sykomora (sycamore fig).

headword: ὁ δὲ ῥητινίτης κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη σκευάζεται ποικίλως
note: Wine with peuke (pine) resin, Galatia; pine species uncertain.
Fresh crushed strobiloi (pine cones) in must; strobilos usually stone pine.

common_name_en: cedar, juniper, cypress, laurel, pine and fir wood wines
note: Several wood wines; first kedros (prickly juniper); arkeuthos, kyparissos, daphne, pitys, elate.
Kedria (cedar pitch) in must; Dsc 1.77 big kedros often read as Lebanon cedar, debated.

headword: ο ἶνος πισσίτης σκευάζεται διὰ πίσσης ὑγρᾶς καὶ γλεύκους
note: Liquid pitch (pissa hygra) from pines in must; species unspecified.
Apsinthion = wormwood; standard identification.
Cilician hyssopos; usually Hyssopus officinalis, some read Origanum syriacum.
Chamaidrys = wall germander; standard identification.
Stoichas = French lavender; standard identification.
Vinegar steeped with stoichas herb.
Kestros psychotrophos = betony; standard identification.
Tragoriganos (goat-marjoram) disputed: Thymus graveolens, Satureja thymbra and others proposed; only family defensible.
Bounion (Dsc 4.123) tentatively Bunium ferulaceum; identification uncertain.
Diktamnon = Cretan dittany; standard identification.
Prasion = white horehound; standard identification.
Thymos usually Thymbra capitata (Coridothymus capitatus).
Thymbra = savory, usually Satureja thymbra.
Origanon Herakleotikon = O. heracleoticum, now Origanum vulgare subsp. hirtum.
Kalaminthe (calamint), glechon (pennyroyal), abrotonon (southernwood) wines made like thyme wine.
Konyza; larger kind usually Dittrichia (Inula) viscosa, smaller D. graveolens.
Multi-ingredient: palm, aspalathos, calamus, Celtic nard and other aromatics.
Multi-ingredient: myrrh, white pepper, iris, dill in wine.
Nektarites from helenion (elecampane); standard identification.

headword: ὁ δὲ διὰ Συριακῆς νάρδου καὶ Κελτικῆς καὶ μαλαβάθρου σκευάζεται οὕτως
note: Multi-ingredient: Syrian nard (Nardostachys), Celtic nard (Valeriana celtica), malabathron; variant with akoron.
Asaron = asarabacca; standard identification.
Dsc 1.10 gives 'wild nard' as synonym of asaron, but separate chapter from asarites; uncertain.
Daukos root; Dsc's chief (Cretan) daukos usually Athamanta cretensis.
Elelisphakos usually Greek sage Salvia fruticosa (S. triloba).
Panax (Herakleion) source of opopanax; usually Opopanax hispidus/chironium.

headword: ἀκορίτης δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ γλυκυρρίζης σκευάζεται ὁμοίως
note: Akoron (sweet flag; some read Iris pseudacorus) and glykyrrhiza (liquorice) wines.
Selinon (garden) seed = celery; standard identification.
Marathon (fennel), anethon (dill), petroselinon wines made alike.
Wine with halos anthos (saline efflorescence); non-plant additive.

headword: γίνεται δὲ καὶ φθόριος ἐμβρύων οἶνος
note: Vines planted with hellebore, wild cucumber or scammony; hellebore kind unspecified.
Thymelaia = Daphne gnidium; standard identification.
Chamelaia usually Cneorum tricoccon (spurge-olive).
Chamaipitys = ground-pine; standard identification.
Root bark of mandragoras; Mediterranean mandrake.
Black helleboros; Greek plant usually H. cyclophyllus, now H. odorus subsp. cyclophyllus; formerly read H. niger.
Skammonia root = scammony; standard identification.
Zinc-oxide-rich furnace deposit from copper smelting (Cyprian botryitis etc.).
Pompholyx/spodos: zinc oxide flue deposits from smelting.
Roasted copper (copper oxides).
Copper oxide flakes formed when molten copper is quenched.

headword: λεπὶς δὲ ἡ μὲν ἐκ τῶν Κυπρίων μετάλλων παχεῖα
note: Hammer scale of copper (helitis); copper oxide flakes.

headword: ἰὸν δὲ τὸν ξυστὸν οὕτως σκευαστέον
note: Ios xystos: copper acetate made with vinegar.
Iron oxide rust.

headword: σκευάζεται καὶ ὁ πεπλυμένος μόλυβδος τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον
note: Lead ground with water in a lead mortar (lead/lead oxides).
Slag of lead smelting.

headword: καὶ ὁ μολυβδοειδὴς δὲ λίθος ἀνάλογον ἔχει τὴν δύναμιν τῇ σκωρίᾳ
note: Molybdoeides lithos; unidentified lead-bearing stone, perhaps galena.
Stibi/larbason: antimony sulfide (stibnite).
Molybdaina: litharge-like lead material, native or from smelting; galena or lead oxide.
Helkysma: slag of silver smelting.
Lithargyros: lead monoxide from silver/lead refining.
Psimythion: basic lead carbonate made with vinegar.
Armenian chrysokolla, deep leek-green; usually malachite.
Armenion: blue copper mineral, usually azurite.
Kyanos from Cyprian copper mines; azurite (some lapis lazuli/Egyptian blue).
Indikon: 'foam of Indian reeds' = indigo; second kind is dyers' scum from vats.
Ochra: yellow iron-oxide earth.

headword: κιννάβαρι οἴονταί τινες τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπάρχειν τῷ καλουμένῳ μινίῳ πλανώμενοι
note: Distinguished from Spanish minium (true cinnabar); costly Libyan kinnabari 'thought dragon's blood', often read as Dracaena resin; debated.
Hydrargyros prepared from minium (cinnabar).
Miltos Sinopike: red iron-oxide ochre.
Sealed medicinal clay from Lemnos (terra sigillata).

headword: χαλκανθὲν τῷ μὲν γένει ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπάρχει
note: Chalkanthon: copper/iron sulfate (blue vitriol).
Copper-iron sulfate ore/weathering product.
Golden, yellow iron sulfate from Cyprus; exact mineral debated (e.g. copiapite).
Black iron-sulfate efflorescence at copper mine mouths.

headword: τὸ δὲ σῶρι ἔνιοι ὑπέλαβον εἶναι μελαντηρίαν πλανώμενοι
note: Sory: impure, foul-smelling sulfate mineral; exact identity uncertain.

headword: τοῦ δὲ διφρυγοῦς τρία οἰητέον εἴδη
note: Roasted copper ore residue/slag, three kinds.
Arsenikon: yellow arsenic sulfide (orpiment).
Sandarake: red arsenic sulfide (realgar).

headword: στυπτηρίας δὲ σχεδὸν πᾶν εἶδος ἐπὶ τῶν αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Αἰγύπτῳ μετάλλων εὐρίσκεται
note: Egyptian stypteria: alum and related astringent sulfates.
Theion: native sulfur.
Kiseris: pumice.
Hales: rock and sea salt kinds.
Halos achne: foamy salt deposit on rocks.
Halme: brine.
Saffron-coloured, fetid saline scum on Nile lakes; possibly microbial; identity uncertain.
Nitron: natural sodium carbonate (natron).
Tryx: lees of old wine, also burnt.
Asbestos (titanos): lime from burnt whelk shells or stones.
Gypsos: gypsum/plaster.
Tephra klematine: ash of vine shoots.

headword: τοῦ δὲ ἀλκυονίου πέντε γνωστέον εἴδη ὑπάρχειν
note: Five kinds of marine sponge-like organisms (sponges, bryozoans, soft corals).
Salty crust on reeds in Galatian marshes ('lake alcyonium'); mineral or organic, unidentified.
Bath sponges (Spongia spp.), male and female kinds.
Kouralion/lithodendron: red coral, Corallium rubrum.
Black branching coral, order Antipatharia.
Dyers' stone from Cappadocia; identity uncertain.
Light porous stone of Assos (volcanic tuff) and its saline efflorescence.
Copper-bearing pyrites (pyrite/chalcopyrite).
Haimatites: haematite iron ore.
Iberian saffron-coloured fissile stone; fibrous haematite/limonite.

headword: τοῦ δὲ γαγάτου προκριτέον τὸν ταχέως ἐξαπτόμενον καὶ ἀσφαλτίζοντα ἐν τῇ ὀσμῇ
note: Gagates: jet (lignite), bitumen-smelling when burnt.
Burns with water, quenched by oil, like gagates; bituminous mineral, uncertain.
Magnes: lodestone attracting iron.
Ivory-like stone, unidentified; chapter text also contains galaktites (5.132, milk-stone).
Like galaktites but sweet-juiced; unidentified.
Soft Egyptian stone used to whiten linen; perhaps steatite or fuller's earth.
Alabastrites/onyx: calcite alabaster.
Greenish, jasper-like Ethiopian stone; unidentified.
Lapis judaicus: acorn-shaped ribbed stones, usually fossil sea-urchin spines.
Fibrous Cypriot stone woven into cloth: asbestos.

headword: λίθος σάπφειρος δοκεῖ ὠφελεῖν σκορπιοπλήκτους πινόμενος
note: Ancient sappheiros is lapis lazuli.
Egyptian pebble said to anaesthetise before surgery; unidentified.
White, transparent, light Arabian stone: selenite (crystalline gypsum).
Iaspis: several coloured kinds (jaspers, chalcedonies).
Snake-spotted stone: serpentinite.
Concretions found in sponges.
Marble or Parian stone mixed with bull glue; multi-ingredient.
Shell-like fissile laminated stone; unidentified.
Smyris: emery used by gem engravers.
Sun-heated seashore sand.
Grindings of iron on Naxian whetstone (emery).
Lithos geodes; unidentified earthy stone.
General properties of earths used in medicine.

headword: τῆς μὲν οὖν Ἑρετριάδος γῆς ἡ μέν τίς ἐστι λευκὴ ἐπιτεταμένως ἡ δὲ σποδοειδής
note: Clay from Eretria, white and ash-coloured kinds.
White clay from Samos.
Stone in Samian earth used by goldsmiths for polishing.
White clay from Chios.
Cimolian earth (fuller's earth) from Kimolos.
Clay resembling Eretrian earth; unlocated.
Fired clay sherds from ovens.
Earth from Melos.
Black bituminous earth (pharmakitis) of Seleucia, used on vines.
Painters' soot from glassworks.
Soot with gum, bull glue and chalkanthon; multi-ingredient.
